2607.23290.title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning
2607.23290.paper_summary: Rare diseases collectively affect an estimated 3.5% to 5.9% of the population, yet more than 70% of patients are misdiagnosed and many endure years of evaluation before a diagnosis is reached, because early presentations are nonspecific and relevant expertise is scarce and unevenly distributed. Artificial intelligence could provide support, but existing systems address isolated stages of care, overwhelmingly diagnosis. They typically depend on the results of downstream investigations, and they treat the variability between models as noise to be eliminated. Here we present RareLens, a system that supports clinical decision-making across the entire rare disease trajectory by exploiting this variability. When heterogeneous large language models evaluate the same case, they generate divergent but complementary reasoning, which RareLens aligns and calibrates into a single convergent, actionable decision at each stage. Four coordinated modules perform primary-visit risk screening, diagnosis, treatment planning and prognosis. Developed and evaluated on RareBench, a real-world dataset of 157,525 cases spanning all 33 Orphanet categories and more than 7,000 conditions, RareLens outperformed every frontier model tested, including GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet and Gemini-2.5-Pro, at each stage. It achieved an area under the curve of 0.917 for screening and top-1 accuracies of 65.5% and 89.8% for diagnosis and treatment. In an external study spanning 1,287 cases and 23 physicians, autonomous RareLens and physicians assisted by RareLens both substantially outperformed unaided physicians. These findings indicate that aligning divergent model reasoning, rather than scaling a single model, offers a generalizable strategy for high-uncertainty clinical decision-making.
2607.23290.paper_summary_zh: 罕見疾病總體上影響約 3.5% 至 5.9% 的人口，但超過 70% 的患者被誤診，許多人在確診之前經歷了多年的評估，因為早期症狀不具特異性，相關專業知識稀缺且分佈不均。人工智慧可以提供支持，但現有系統僅針對孤立的護理階段，主要集中於診斷。它們通常依賴於下游調查的結果，並將模型之間的變異性視為需要消除的噪音。在此，我們介紹 RareLens，一個通過利用這種變異性來支持整個罕見疾病過程中臨床決策的系統。當異質的大型語言模型評估相同的案例時，它們會產生不同但互補的推理，RareLens 將這些推理對齊並校準為每個階段的一個單一收斂、可行的決策。四個協調模塊執行初診風險篩查、診斷、治療計劃和預後。在 RareBench 上開發和評估，這是一個涵蓋所有 33 個 Orphanet 類別和超過 7,000 種病症的 157,525 例案例的真實世界數據集，RareLens 在每個階段的表現超過了所有測試的前沿模型，包括 GPT-5、DeepSeek-R1、Claude-3.7-Sonnet 和 Gemini-2.5-Pro。它在篩查中達到了 0.917 的曲線下面積，在診斷和治療中分別達到了 65.5% 和 89.8% 的 top-1 準確率。在一項涵蓋 1,287 例案例和 23 名醫生的外部研究中，自主的 RareLens 和由 RareLens 協助的醫生均顯著超過了未經協助的醫生。這些發現表明，對齊不同模型的推理，而不是擴展單一模型，提供了一種可普遍應用的高不確定性臨床決策策略。
